summary.intent: Continue managing PR #615 (Phase 80 of the CipherBox v2.0 milestone) — verify greptile's flagged security concern and then plan and fix the discovered web file-grant re-mint gap directly within the PR.
summary.outcome: Traced greptile's P1 to a real, pre-existing (not Phase-80-caused) gap where separately-shared files inside owner-rotated folders never get their grant re-minted on web, correctly resolved the mis-traced thread, then implemented and unit-tested a fix: an optional `resolveInlineGrantRemint` seam threaded through client.ts and wired in web's owner-reconcile/rotation-driver services, reusing the sdk-core inline re-mint mechanism already used by desktop/Rust. Core fix + unit tests are green and committed; an sdk-e2e round-trip test is still to be delegated.

repo: The sdk-core inline grant-remint seam (`rotateOne` → `reMintGrantsRootedAt(nodeId, key, gen, ..., node.kind)`) was already fully built and file-aware, but web's `performScopeExitRotation` always passed `innerGrants: undefined, grantCallbacks: undefined`, so it never fired — web relied entirely on the `owner-reconcile` sweep, which skips file roots at the folderTree gate, leaving shared-file grants never re-minted after folder rotation.
Desktop (Rust) rotation re-mints grants inline with `node.kind`, which is why desktop e2e stayed green while the web path silently had the gap.

Cross-package TS builds go stale silently: after Phase 80 added `recipientPins` to `NodeWriteBody` in `@cipherbox/core`, `packages/sdk` typecheck failed with missing-symbol errors until `core` then `sdk-core` dist were rebuilt bottom-up, then `sdk` dist, then `apps/web` typecheck — the fix is a bottom-up dist rebuild, not a source bug.

`tests/sdk-e2e` test harness (`fixtures/test-harness.ts`) does not wire `rotationCallbacks` at all — rotation is effectively a no-op there today, so proving inline re-mint behavior currently must go through the sdk chokepoint unit test (`client-rotation.test.ts`), not the sdk-e2e suite, unless the harness is extended.

`setupFolder` test helper sets the folder's `nodeId: 'test-node-id'` and returns the child with `id: 'file1'` — relevant when asserting which nodeId a rotation root passes through mocked `rotateReadFromNode` calls.

code.finding: performScopeExitRotation calls rotateReadFromNode with grantCallbacks: undefined, innerGrants: undefined unconditionally — this is why web never re-mints grants inline during rotation; fix wires a resolveInlineGrantRemint callback here instead.

getRecipientPubkeyPins here is folder-only (via requireFolder) and the sweep entry points skip file roots at folderTree.get(shareRootIpnsName) gates (~lines 198-201, 256-257) before this line is ever reached for files — greptile's throw-line claim was technically unreachable but the underlying re-mint gap it pointed at was real.

reMintGrantsRootedAt gates pin enforcement on a nodeKind PARAMETER (const isFile = nodeKind === 'file') rather than deriving it from the node itself — callers must correctly thread node.kind for the file carve-out to apply.

workflow: When re-verifying a reviewer's (greptile) finding, always confirm you're on the actual PR/feature branch first — reading main after a `git checkout main` produced a false 'stale finding' conclusion and led to wrongly resolving a real security thread.

Distinguishing a real pre-existing gap from a Phase-introduced regression changed the merge recommendation materially — worth explicitly tracing 'was this always broken' before treating a finding as in-scope for the current PR.

Dispatching a tightly-scoped, read-only verification subagent for a security-sensitive disputed claim (rather than a third self-trace) surfaced the accurate, evidence-backed verdict and avoided a second wrong resolution.

Before implementing, doing a full read-only mapping pass (types, client seam, web service, sdk-core engine, test harness capabilities) across multiple Read/Bash calls let the fix be scoped to 'web + sdk wiring only' with confidence, avoiding an unnecessarily large multi-package change.

Committing was done in the background per the known 1Password SSH-signing-hang gotcha (a commit can land successfully even though the tool call reports a timeout — verify via git log rather than retrying).

friction: Wasted verification effort from initially reading the wrong git branch (main instead of the feat branch), producing an inaccurate 'greptile is stale' conclusion that was then incorrectly published as a thread resolution.

Stale cross-package dist builds (core → sdk-core → sdk) caused a wall of misleading TypeScript errors that were actually just build staleness, not real type errors, requiring a bottom-up rebuild before typecheck could be trusted.

sdk-e2e test harness doesn't wire rotationCallbacks, so a true end-to-end round-trip proof for the fix isn't currently available without harness changes, forcing reliance on unit-level chokepoint tests as primary proof.
